gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Noto Sans Nushu stands tall, its terminals held well away from the stroke body. And Quilon above it carries a faint stone-carved heft, so the two feel like a carved title over a modern, upright line.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Quilon is a commanding display face whose stems run only a shade heavier than the arms joining them. Noto Sans Ogham below feels tall and sturdy.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Solid, block-like words are what Noto Sans Ol Chiki gives you, with curve tails held well back. Quilon handles the rounded, slightly thickened display letters, while Noto Sans Ol Chiki handles the steady text.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-old-hungarian: Moderate shading across round and straight strokes gives Quilon its editorial, commanding presence, with large open shapes in a, e and s. Noto Sans Old Hungarian stays readable even at tiny sizes.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-old-italic: Quilon brings an editorial, commanding voice, with a modest dip in its thin strokes and a calm ebb and flow of thickness. Noto Sans Old Italic follows with almost no gap between x-height and cap height, which is the strongest thing about the pair.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-old-north-ara: Tall, dense and a bit quirky, this pairing has presence. Quilon shows faint nib-pressure variation in its round letters, and Noto Sans Old North Arabian packs a tight lowercase band with outward-pointing terminals.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-old-permic: Noto Sans Old Permic has rounded forms that stay clearly open to the side, with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals. And Quilon sits above it with slightly thinner joins where curves meet stems, giving a commanding contrast to the approachable text.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-old-persian: Noto Sans Old Persian has a lofty, tall lowercase and counters that breathe into the white space. Noto Sans Old Persian beside Quilon, with its mild contrast, makes a pair whose strongest quality is quiet openness.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-old-turkic: Each bowl in Quilon carries a light swell, like pressed glass, under its editorial manner. Noto Sans Old Turkic answers with chunky, tall lowercase and open-mouthed curves, so the strongest quality here is sturdy clarity.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Restful is the word for Quilon, whose line swings only modestly in weight while still sounding commanding. Noto Sans Oriya brings generous curve gaps and small letters almost as tall as the capitals, so the strongest quality is easy openness.
